work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. I.

items.text: Provide for them a thankful recompense as they have need and as you are able and have opportunity.
items.citation: Cobbett, Honour due from Children, CHAP. I.
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother, i.e. as they need, and as thou art able, & hast opportunity, make them thankfull recompence

items.text: Conduct yourself so as to be an honor to them, bringing no disgrace upon their name.
items.citation: Cobbett, Honour due from Children, CHAP. I.
items.quote: be an honour to them, carry it so, as may redound to their honour, and no way to their disgrace.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Give your parents an eminent and transcendent honour, next to the honour due to God; do not scant or slight them, but give them their full weight and measure.
items.citation: Rogers, Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II
items.quote: It sheweth evidently, that it is no ordinary measure of Honour, which Children owe to their Parents

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Honor both father and mother equally; do not prefer one over the other in love, reverence, obedience, or recompense.
items.citation: Discourse, Chap. II
items.quote: The Father is not to be preferred by the Child as a Child, before the Mother; or the Mother more loved, reverenced, obeyed or recompensed then the Father.

items.text: Honor your parents sincerely and from the heart, not merely with outward show or pretense.
items.citation: Discourse, Chap. II
items.quote: It must not be a bare pretended, and formall kind of Honour of Parents.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. I.

items.text: Honor your father and mother, and fear them, as the Lord commands.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. I.
items.quote: Ye shall fear every man his Mother, and every man his Father, and keep my Sabbaths.

items.text: Requite your parents: repay them for their care.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. I.
items.quote: let them learn of shew piety to them at home, and to requite their Parents

items.text: Command your children to keep the way of the Lord, to do judgment and justice.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. I.
items.quote: I know Abraham, that he will command his children,—and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do judgement and justice.

items.text: Hearken to your parents' counsel and rebukes; do not despise them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. I.
items.quote: the good counsels which our fathers, or our mothers gave us, but, wretches that we were, we would never hearken to them, nor regard them.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Honor your father and mother from the heart, not merely in outward show.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: My Son, give me thy heart

items.text: Honor your father and mother all your life, even when they are old or weak; do not despise your mother when she is old.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: despise not thy Mother when she is old

items.text: Honor your father and mother with all your being: heart, eyes, thoughts, and body.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: My Son, give me thy heart, and let thine eyes observe my wayes

items.text: Honor your father and mother equally whether they are poor or rich, gentle or harsh, as Christ was subject to his poor parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: the command of God knoweth no persons, distinguisheth not of such a Father, or such and such a Mother

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Do not honor your father or mother with selfish, self-ended motives, such as hope of gain or furthering your own desires.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Look that it be not a base selfish, self-ended Honouring of Father, or Mother, for hope of gain by them

items.text: Honor your father and mother whether they are poor or rich, high or low, with nothing to give or much to leave.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother, namely poor or rich, high or low

items.text: Honor your parents from a heart of entire love to them, not from love to yourself.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: our honour, which we give to our Parents, be not from love to our selves, but it is from intire love to them

items.text: Honor them out of love to God, recognizing in them the image of his fatherhood.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: the love of whom especially, should put Children upon Honouring the Image of his Father-hood, in their Parents

items.text: Honor them willingly and filially, not slavishly from fear of punishment or correction.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: it is a slavish, and not a filiall Honouring of them

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Obey their counsels and commands, but do not obey them when it would dishonor God by neglecting his requirements or doing what he forbids.
items.citation: Cobbet, Honour due from Children, Chap. 2
items.quote: Children must indeed honour their Parents Counsels and Commands with the honour of obedience and observance, yet not so as in a way of dishonour to God

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Do not despise or slight your parents when they are old or decayed in strength or estate.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parent, CHAP. II
items.quote: despise not thy Mother when she is old

items.text: Obey your parents' commands from the heart, not merely with words.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parent, CHAP. II
items.quote: he saith, I go Sir, but went not

items.text: Do not disgrace, reproach, or expose the shame of your parents.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parent, CHAP. II
items.quote: discover his Fathers nakedness to his reproach

items.text: Do not curse or revile your parents; instead bless them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parent, CHAP. II
items.quote: There is a generation that curseth their Father, and doth not bless their Mother

items.text: Receive your parents' counsel and correction, and follow their godly example.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parent, CHAP. II
items.quote: they cared not for his counsels, or checks, or imitation of his godly course

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Listen to your father's and mother's instruction and do not despise their reproofs and corrections.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: A wise son heareth his fathers instructions.

items.text: Obey your parents' commands, especially your mother's; do not despise them.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: The eye that despiseth to obey his Mother

items.text: Remain under your parents' watch and government until you are ready and called to leave; do not wander away.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: As a bird that wandreth from her neast, so is a man that wandereth from his place

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your parents, for this is to honor them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: children are to Honour their Parents with the Honour of obedience.

items.text: Be content to be set about the meanest employments, even as though you were a servant, when your parents require it.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: childrens being content to be set about meanest imployments, even as though they were servants, their Parents so requiring it

items.text: Be content to have your own desires and ways crossed, and yield to your parents' minds and wills in things lawful.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: Childrens being content to be crossed in their own desires or wayes, and to yeeld to and obey Parents minds and wils, in matters lawfull

items.text: Yield especially to your parents' minds in the matter of marriage.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: yeedling especially to Parents minds in the matter of marriage

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. I.

items.text: Honor your father and mother: highly prize, respect, and dearly love them as parents.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother, i.e. highly prise and respect, and most dearly love thy Father & thy mother

items.text: Reverence and awe your father and mother as parents, giving them the honor of fear.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: Honour thy Father and thy Mother i.e. reverence and awe them

items.text: Obey your father and mother, showing your honor in all acts of obedience.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: if to Honour Father and Mother then to obey them, for obedience is, in part, the honor due to them

items.text: Recompense your father and mother, repaying them as honor demands.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: Honour of Recompence

items.text: Honor your husband as your superior by private contract, as the commandment requires honor to all superiors.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: Husbands who are wives superiours

items.text: Honor your master as a father, giving him the respect due to one in authority.
items.citation: Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. I
items.quote: Masters... are as Fathers to their Servants, Scholars, and Pupils.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. IV. Of Honour of Reverence due from children to Parents.

items.text: Rise and stand bare before them when they come to you or speak to you.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: Children are to rise up and to stand bare before their Parents, when they come to them, or speak to them

items.text: Go out to meet them when they are coming toward you.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: If Parents be comming towards children, they are to prevent them, and meet them

items.text: Bow to them as an act of reverence.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: they are to bow to them

items.text: Speak reverently to them and about them to others.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They must speak Reverently both to their Parents, and of them to others.

items.text: Attend reverently to their counsels and instructions.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are to attend reverently to their counsels, or instructions

items.text: Submit meekly and humbly to their seasonable corrections.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They must meekly and humbly subject themselves to their seasonable corrections

items.text: Show filial shame and blush, and confess humbly when you have sinned against them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: To express filial shame and blushing to Parents, upon occasion of faults and sins against them

items.text: Own their persons, parental relation, and authority in your heart.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are inwardly to own the very persons and parentall relations, and Authority of their Parents

items.text: Awe their commands, reproofs, threats, and corrections with a filial, not slavish, fear.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are inwardly to awe the commands, reproofs, threats and corrections of Parents

items.text: Fear to lose their favor or incur their just displeasure by giving them offense.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are inwardly to fear to lose parents favour, or to incur their just displeasure

items.text: Fear to cross any weighty intent, purpose, or desire of theirs, especially in sacred matters.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are to fear to cross any weighty intents, purposes, or desires of parents, especially when in sacred matters

items.text: Fear to occasion trouble or heart-grief to them if you can prevent it.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. IV
items.quote: They are to fear that trouble or heart-grief should be occasioned to parents, if they can prevent it.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your parents in all things, for this is right and pleasing to God; you owe them obedience as a debt all your days.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. V
items.quote: Children obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing to the Lord... children owe obedience to their Parents as a debt

items.text: Do not merely say you will obey, but actually do what your parents command, and do it readily and promptly.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. V
items.quote: in shew express obedience to your Parents commands, but in reality do it not

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Give your commands to your children in the most moving expressions, that they may attend and obey.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V.4
items.quote: Use holy wisdome in giving your parentall commands... in the most moving expressions, which may help on affectionate attendance and observance

items.text: Yield to the just desires of your children, that you may win their willing obedience.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V.5
items.quote: Do you readily yeeld to the just desires even of your children, and it will notably prevail with your children most readily to yeeld to any just commands of yours

items.text: Listen to the good advice your children give you in a fitting manner, and so win their obedient submission.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V.6
items.quote: hearken to the good advice, which even your children do seasonably, and in a suitable manner give to you, and this also will exceedingly win your childrens hearts to an obedientiall submission

items.text: Obey your parents from the heart, for this is the real honour you owe them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: Behold, to obey is better then sacrifice, and to harken then the fat of Ramms.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Be effectually solicitous of your parents' outward safety and good in times of danger and straits; interpose between them and danger, even at the hazard of your own life, and repay like for like.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents
items.quote: Let children recompence parents by being effectually sollicitous of their parents outward safety and good in times of danger and straits

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. III. Of Honour in speciall due to Parents, and that in a direct way, and therein of Honour of respect and love due to Parents.

items.text: Treat your children as children, not as slaves for your profit, and do not put them off basely after you have used them.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: making thereby your Children more like slaves for your profits, then Children, & as basely putting them off

items.text: Keep just promises made to your children, especially in matters of disposing them in marriage.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: By breaking just promises made, respecting your Children, especially, in matters of disposall of them in marriage

items.text: Do not force your children into marriages against their lawful affections or for base ends.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: forcing of matches for sinister and low ends upon your Children, crosse to the very bent of their minds

items.text: Do not misplace your affections upon unworthy children; love all your children impartially.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: By misplacing your respects upon unworthy Children, as Isaac upon Esau

items.text: Cherish, strengthen, and enlarge your respect and love toward your parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: To Children, to cherrish, strengthen, and inlarge your respect and love to your Parents

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Learn to show piety at home and requite your parents, especially when they are in need.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: let them, that is the Adult Children of such ancient widdowes, learn to shew piety; (or kindnesse) at home, and to requite their parents

items.text: Serve your parents and labour for their good and maintenance, as Christ served his earthly parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: Jesus Christ, when on earth, he wrought hard with his reputed Father, for the maintenance of his poor Mother

items.text: Repay your parents as much as you can for their past care and labour, recognizing their love and sacrifices.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: there must be a thankful retaliation, as much as may be, though perfectly and fully it cannot be

items.text: If your grandparent is a widow in need, learn to show piety and requite her.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: if any Widdow have Children, or Nephewes, let them... learn to shew piety... and to requite their parents

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Serve your parents with good will and freeness, not grudgingly, as they served you.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: Children, do you the like for them; even servants are to serve their Masters with good will... Much more should children do so, in what you do for your parents.

items.text: Serve your parents constantly and willingly, without needing to be urged or watched, and without counting what you have done for them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: Parents never needed urging, or forcing... let children do like for like: let none... need to urge you... but let it be as a very naturall fruit, arising freely... Parents needed no eye of man... let children do like for like; very servants to Masters, should not do eye service...

items.text: Maintain your aged, decrepit parents with all that you can.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: it would be a monstrous thing, if children should not now do all that ever they can to maintain these their decayed, decrepit, exhausted parents

items.text: Condescend to the meanest services for your parents when they need them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VI
items.quote: Parents... condescended to meanest offices... let children do like for like for parents, as they may have use, or stand in need of them.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. IV. Of Honour of Reverence due from children to Parents.

items.text: Fear to fall short of your parents' blessing and prayers, and heed their godly counsel.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Honour of Reverence 6
items.quote: They are to fear to fall short of their blessing, and benefit of parents prayers, and of their godly parentall wishes and Counsels.

items.text: Be inwardly ashamed when you give your parents just cause for displeasure; confess your fault and unworthiness.
items.citation: Gouge, Of Honour of Reverence 7
items.quote: They are also to be inwardly, as well as outwardly ashamed, that parents have just cause of distaste against them at any time.

items.text: Do not be rude or irreverent in your gestures or speech before your parents.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: how rudely do they sit before their parents, and how irreverently do they carry it, in their gestures before them?

items.text: Do not interrupt your parents while they are speaking; wait quietly for them to finish.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: how forward are they to prevent or interrupt their parents in speaking

items.text: Do not answer back or rebuke your parents when they correct you.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: or to answer them again if rebuked by them

items.text: Do not act over-familiar with your parents as if no difference existed between parent and child.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: how over-familiar do too many children make themselves with their parents? as if hail-fellow well met

items.text: Do not carry yourself proudly, disdainfully, or scornfully toward your parents.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: yea too many there are, who carry it proudly, disdainfully and scornfully towards parents

items.text: Do not grumble, contest, or contend against your parents' commands, counsel, or correction.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: ready to mutter and grumble at their parents counsels, commands, just threats, rebukes, or corrections

items.text: Dread your parents' commands, prohibitions, reproofs, and corrections; fear losing their favor and blessing.
items.citation: Gouge, CHAP. IV
items.quote: how little also do too many children dread their parents commands, counsels, prohibitions, reproofs, or corrections? how little do they fear the loss of their favour or blessing

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Honor your father and mother in the Lord, from conscience to God and obedience to his command.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Children obey your Parents in the Lord

items.text: Relieve your parents in their need; do not let any religious vow or gift excuse you from this debt.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: they needed not to relieve them... that would exempt them... from relieving their Parents

items.text: Hold up your parents' honor when they are aged or infirm; cover their failings as Shem and Japhet covered Noah's nakedness.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Shem, and Japhet took a garment, and laid it upon their shoulders, and went backwards, and covered the nakedness of their Father

items.text: Thirst after your parents' souls welfare and seek to lead them out of idolatry as Abraham did for Terah.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Abraham, what in him lay, to help out his Idolatrous Father Terah, from his course and way

items.text: Be as willing and joyful to honor your parents as you are to be honored or benefited by them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: as willing and joyfull to Honour Parents... as they are to have it be well with them here or hereafter

items.text: Do not soon forget your parents after they are dead; mourn their death and remember them, as Isaac mourned Sarah.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: For three years space then, this pious Son was ever and anon mourning in thoughts of his good Mothers death

items.text: Prevent whatever may corrupt or discourage your children in the fear and worship of God.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Take very speciall care, to prevent whatsoever, either may corrupt them, or any wayes discourage them in the matter of the Honour of God himself, or of his word.

items.text: Redress disorderly carriages among your children towards one another, lest they learn to dishonor you.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Redress what in you lyeth... disorderly carriages of your Children towards one another

items.text: Be fearers and honorers of God yourselves, that your children may be blessed with a spirit of honor toward parents.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Labour to be fearers and honourers of God your selves... that your Children shall be blessed

items.text: Pray much and plead earnestly with God for your children, that he would write his law in their hearts.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Pray much and plead earnestly with God for your Children, that God would write his Law... in their hearts

items.text: Act your faith upon the promises of God for your children's best welfare.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Act your faith upon the promises of God, undertaking for your Childrens best welfare

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.
items.quote: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your parents especially in the things of God, which they command you in God's name for your soul's welfare.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: in obeying chiefly in things of God, as injoyned to children, in Gods name, by their Parents; whether respecting the knowledge of God in Christ, mortification, or in any other means, or parts of the souls welfare.

items.text: Submit humbly, meekly, and quietly to your parents' just reproofs and corrections.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: In childrens yeelding humbly, meekly and quietly to Parents just reproofs and corrections, Heb. 12. 9. The Fathers of our flesh corrected us and we gave them reverence.

items.text: Obey your parents in all things that are lawful, without exception or limitation.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: Children obey your Parents in all things, one as well as another, being all lawfull: there is no exception, or limitation made.

items.text: Obey your parents diligently, sparing no pains in their service.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: as a Son with the Father he hath served with me in the Gospel, i. e. very diligently: so Jacobs sons followed their Fathers business diligently, sparing no pains

items.text: Obey your parents readily and cheerfully, as soon as they command.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: Come, I will send thee to thy brethren, saith Jacob to Joseph; here am I saith Joseph, he is as ready to do it, as his Father to command it.

items.text: Do not let others' frowns or flattering persuasions turn you from lawful obedience to your parents.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: Children are not to be diverted from lawfull obedience to Parents, either by frowns, or flattering perswasions of others

items.text: Obey your parents conscientiously, as unto God, for their parental authority is from God.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: to parentall Authority as of God, and as to Gods command requiring it of you to Honour Father and Mother

items.text: Command your children to keep the way of the Lord.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: I know Abraham that he will command his children, and they shall keep the way of the Lord.

items.text: Correct and chasten your children for their good, as God's appointed means to rescue them from sin and ruin.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, Chap. V
items.quote: Chasten thy Son, while there is hope, and withhold not correction from the child... thou shalt beat him, and deliver his soul from Hell.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Avoid self-will, conceit, discontent, envy of siblings, bad company, and dwelling on your parents' weaknesses, for these breed stubbornness toward them.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. V
items.quote: Take heed of such things as hinder filial obedience, and breed and feed stubbornesse in you to your parents; such as self-conceitednesse, self-willednesse...

items.text: If you have been disobedient, confess it humbly to your parents and ask pardon, as the prodigal did to his father.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. V
items.quote: bewayle the same, and humbly to confess the same, as to God, so to your wronged parents, if yet living

items.text: When God stirs you by his word or correcting providences, do not stifle or delay; return to obedience to your parents at once.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. V
items.quote: look to it that you do not stifle those movings, nor suppresse those workings of heart, nor procrastinate and put off the real practising of such counsels

items.text: Give them your heart: love, fear, and reverence them, so you will be ready to obey them.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. V
items.quote: My Son, saith Solomon, give me thine heart; and let thine eyes observe my waies, Prov. 23. 26.

items.text: Set before you the obedient lives of Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Christ, and the punishment of disobedient children, to spur you to obey your parents.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. V
items.quote: set before your eyes the examples of persons eminent for filial obedience; as Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Jesus Christ, who also was subject to his Parents

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your father and mother in all things according to God, as Jacob obeyed his father and mother.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: The Children, in obedience to their parents commands, under God, they must observe to do all the words of that Law.

items.text: Lay your authority upon your children and require of them obedience to all God's commands.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: They must lay their authority upon their Children, to require of them also obedience to all Gods Commands.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. III. Of Honour in speciall due to Parents, and that in a direct way, and therein of Honour of respect and love due to Parents.

items.text: Plead respectfully with them to turn from sin, as Jonathan did with his father.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: Plead with your Mother, plead saith God to the good Children of the Church: Children may in such a way, and must plead with their very Mothers.

items.text: Sympathize with them in their joys and sorrows, and comfort them in grief.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: They are cordially to symphathize with their Parents in their joyes or sorrows

items.text: Have natural affection for them, honoring them with respect and love.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: do any such as you are, honour Parents with the Honour of respect and love?

items.text: Be trustworthy with their counsels, secrets, estates, and occasions, not treacherous.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: Such as Parents know not how to trust with their Counsels, Secrets, Estates, or occasions, they are so false to them

items.text: Do not draw them into sin, as Lot's daughters did.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: Some will cunningly draw their very Parents into some sinfull snares

items.text: Provide for them in their needs; do not neglect them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: Some neglect to do for them in their needs

items.text: Do not revile, strike, or scoff at them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: Some there are who are ready to give reviling speeches to their Parents, Exod. 21. to strike at them, ibid. or to scoffe at them, Prov. 30 17.

items.text: Do not waste their estate or break their hearts by lewd courses.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: to imbesil or wast their estates, Pro. 19. 26.

items.text: Avoid gross sins that would bring a curse upon your children and alienate their affection.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: By committing some heinous sin against God, against your Parents, or against others, and so bring this as a curse upon your Children to be so unnaturall

items.text: Do not be churlish, harsh, bitter, or cruel in your corrections, lest you alienate their hearts.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren, CHAP. III
items.quote: too many Churlish, harsh and strange carriages, bitter and reviling speeches, unmercifull and cruell correctings, and punishings of them

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. III. Of Honour in speciall due to Parents, and that in a direct way, and therein of Honour of respect and love due to Parents.

items.text: Deny yourself for your parents' good: stay with them in want and weakness, work and take risks for them rather than forsake them.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: Children are to deny themselves for their Parents choise good... they must be willing to suffer and lose somewhat with them, and for them, rather then forsake them.

items.text: Stay with a needy mother-in-law, work hard to supply her, rather than leave for better prospects.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: she will not leave her though a younger Woman... she will work hard for her... to bring in supplies to her Mother-in-law.

items.text: Be deeply affected by your parents' love and just displeasure; let their favor or frowns move you greatly.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: They are to be exceedingly affected with their Parents true love to them, or grounded and just displeasure against them

items.text: Prize your parents' counsels, instructions, and even rebukes; keep their words in your heart.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: They are to prize very much Parents good and savoury Counsels and instructions, yea, their very rebukes

items.text: Love your brothers and sisters dearly, for you bear your parents' common image.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: they are to cleave to Brethren and Sisters of the same Parents, 1 Pet. 3, 8. Love as Brethren

items.text: Meekly and wisely dissuade your parents from all that would endanger their souls.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Parents, CHAP. III
items.quote: They are meekly and wisely to use all faithfull endeavours, to disswade Parents, and to take them off, from whatsoever might indanger their very souls welfare

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your parents in all lawful commands and instructions.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: children... will not be counselled, commanded, reproved, or corrected by Parents

items.text: Receive your parents' counsel, reproof, and correction humbly; do not be stubborn or persistent in disobedience.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: they hearkened not to the voyce of their Father... because the Lord would slay them

items.text: Follow your parents' direction in choosing an honest calling or course of life.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: would have them of an honest calling, or course of life... yet will not be ruled

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent; listen to their counsel against ungodly matches.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: Is there never a daughter among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistins?

items.text: If you have been disobedient, repent and return to obedience.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: like that Son in the Parable... who repenting of that stubborn answer to his Father... but after he repented and went

items.text: Do not abuse your authority by commanding your children unlawful or unjust things.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: abusing their authority in giving out unjust commands

items.text: Correct and reprove your children for their faults; do not be over-indulgent.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: the rod and reproof giveth wisdome, but a child left to himself... bringeth his Mother to shame

items.text: Set a godly example by your own obedience to God, so as not to provoke your children to disobedience.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: By your own rebellion against Gods commands... God in judgement leaveth children to be rebellious against you

items.text: Counsel your children against ungodly marriages.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. V
items.quote: when his Parents wisely and faithfully replyed... Is there never a daughter among all my people

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. III. Of Honour in speciall due to Parents, and that in a direct way, and therein of Honour of respect and love due to Parents.

items.text: Delight greatly in your father's presence; be much affected with the very sight of your father or mother.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: They are to be delighted greatly in their Fathers presence, to be much affected with the very sight of a Father or Mother.

items.text: Do not be forward to part with your parents; part only when God's special call or providence forces you.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: They are not forward to part with their Parents, but as urged & in a sort forced by any speciall call or providence of God

items.text: If you must be absent, long for their company again in a moderate and regular way.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: if sometimes called, to be absent from them for a time, yet to be longing (in a moderate and regular way) after their Company againe.

items.text: If your parent dies, grieve deeply; a motherless child's mourning is the saddest of mournings.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: a Mother-Iess Childs mourning then, for a deceased Mother, is the saddest of mournings

items.text: Cling to your mother-in-law and refuse to leave her; share her lot in wealth and woe, and let only death part you.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: Ruth clave to her... Intreat me not to leave thee, for whither thou goest I will go, and where thou lodged I will lodge.

items.text: Before you depart on a calling, kiss your father and mother in affectionate farewell.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: Elisha must needs go and kiss his Father and Mother

items.text: If you are taken away from your home, bewail your father and mother for a full month.
items.citation: Gouge, Domesticall Duties, Chap. 3
items.quote: God will have the poore captive Woman, when her Master liketh her for his Wife, yet to bewaile her Father and Mother for a Moneth

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Honor your parents; do not be unnatural, irreverent, disobedient, or ungrateful toward them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: you may thank your selves, if you have unnatural, irreverent, disobedient, or ingratefull Children

items.text: Do not bring God's judgment upon your children and posterity by daring sins against God or man.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: By bringing any just blast upon their Children and posterity, through some other daring sins against God or man

items.text: Give your children a careful and pious education, not rude, profane, or worldly.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: By neglect of good and pious education of children; when Parents bring up their Children rudely and profanely, carnally, and carelesly

items.text: Do not humour your children in their lusts, pride, or voluptuousness.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: By foolish humouring of their Children in their lusts: either in their Pride, or voluptuousness

items.text: Do not provoke your children to wrath by harsh, austere, or rigid carriage; do not discourage them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: Fathers (saith he) provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged

items.text: Live peaceably with your wife; avoid discord, hard speeches, and cross carriages, lest you undermine your authority before your children.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: By discords, and uncomfortable breaches, hard speeches, cross carriages, and discontents, betwixt Fathers and Mothers

items.text: Do not be contentious with your husband; a contentious wife is a continual dropping that undermines the household.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: the contentions of a Wife are a continuall dropping

items.text: Break your children's headstrong wills; do not leave them to their own desires.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: By suffering Children too much to have their wills, and not seasonably and frequently to break them of their own head-strong wills

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Do not marry an unbeliever or one outside the faith, for it dishonors your parents and their Christian profession.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: Such Children as match dishonourably to your Parents, even to your Christian Parents profession, and gracious interests

items.text: Avoid bringing reproach or censure upon your parents by unworthy marriages.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: your Parents come hereby to suffet reproach

items.text: Do not allow your spouse to hinder you from honoring, reverencing, obeying, and recompensing your parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: bad Husbands will be hindring the wives due respect to her good Parents, or any due reverence, or filiall obedience, or filiall recompence

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. III. Of Honour in speciall due to Parents, and that in a direct way, and therein of Honour of respect and love due to Parents.

items.text: Do not be unnatural to your parents; shun the vices that breed it: ignorance of God, self-love, covetousness, pride, and love of pleasure.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Take heed of any leading causes which breed and feed unnaturalness... such as are, 1. Ignorance... 2. Self-love... 3. A worldly, covetous Spirit... 4. A proud Spirit... 5. A Voluptuous Spirit

items.text: Love your parents, but do not approve of their evil sayings, principles, or practices.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Look that it be not such as to approve of the evill saiyings, principles, or practises of your ungodly, or of your seducing or seduced Parents.

items.text: Do not follow your parents' sinful counsel in anything.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Let it not be such, as to follow their evill Counsell in any thing

items.text: When your parents plot evil, do not keep their counsel, but reveal it seasonably.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Let it not be so as to keep their dangerous and wicked Counsel, in any way of wickednesse, but rather seasonably to reveal it

items.text: When God calls you to it, bear witness against your parents' sin—even in gross idolatry or seduction from the Lord.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: when you are called of God to it, then not to bear seasonable witnesse against their sin, as in case of Parents seducing Children from the Lord and his worship, In case of grosse Idolatry

items.text: When married, do not for your parents' sake neglect just respects to your spouse and family.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: when you are called to maried conditions, then for Parents sakes, to neglect just respects to your spouses, and regard to your Families welfare

items.text: Frequently instruct your children in the best things, especially their soul's welfare.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Be frequently instructing your Children in the best things, in their Soul-matters

items.text: Encourage your children in every good thing.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Be ever and anon incouraging your Children in any good thing

items.text: Be ready to defend and vindicate your children in any just cause.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Be ready to defend, and vindicate Children in any just cause

items.text: Be careful and solicitous for your children's outward welfare.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Be conscionable, sollicitous of your childrens outward welfare

items.text: Show tender compassion to your children, as need and prudence require.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. III
items.quote: Carry it towards your children with much tenderness and bowels, as need and prudence requireth

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Comfort your father and mother in all their sorrows, losses, and sufferings; cheer their spirits when they are ready to fail.
items.citation: Cobbet, Honour due from Children, CHAP. VI
items.quote: let children cheer them up all they can... Let children be as so many Noahs, comforts, and comforters, against whatsoever miseries, or calamities which may befall their parents

items.text: Be a cherisher, succourer, and supporter to your grandmother in her old age, easing her faintings and troubles.
items.citation: Cobbet, Honour due from Children, CHAP. VI
items.quote: the grand-child Boaz, must be his grand-mothers cherisher, succourer, and supporter, under God, against all her faintings, sinkings, and troubles of her elder times

items.text: Love your mother-in-law and be her succour, supporter, and comforter, as dear to her as many sons.
items.citation: Cobbet, Honour due from Children, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Ruth is such a succourer, and supporter, and comforter to her, that she is instead of many Sons

items.text: Be to your parents as eyes when they are dim-sighted, strength when weak, feet when lame, nourishment when needy, and a staff to their age.
items.citation: Cobbet, Honour due from Children, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Children should be as eyes to their dim-sighted parents, as strength to them when weak, Feet to them when lame

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Watch over your children and keep a wise, straight hand over them before they grow stiff and inflexible.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.
items.quote: keep a wise and straight hand over them, and that in time

items.text: Provide seasonably and suitably for your children in marriage.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.
items.quote: provide not seasonably and suitably for your Children in Marriage

items.text: Do not lay up ill-gotten goods, lest your children be exposed to reproachful courses and you to shame.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.
items.quote: lay up ill gotten goods, as gain of oppression, deceit, violence, or any injustice

items.text: Do not distill corrupt principles of religion into your children, nor suffer others to do so.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.
items.quote: suffer others, yea it may be too forward your selves to be distilling into them corrupt principles of Religion

items.text: Do not be a dishonor to your parents; do not reflect dishonor upon them.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.
items.quote: even you are every way a dishonour to your parents, and reflect and put much dishonour upon them

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Conduct yourself as an honor to your parents: as olive plants, arrows, builders, and polished stones, so live as to bring them glory and not shame.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: their work is to contrive, compose, advance, adorn, replenish, or occasionally to repair that goodly piece, their Parents Honour

items.text: Do not expose your children to dishonorable practices or temptations; guard them from evil.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: you unadvisedly expose your Children to dishonourable practices, or temptations thereunto

items.text: Do not bind your children by rash vows or engagements that ensnare them, such as vows of celibacy; seek their freedom and well-being.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: ingaging of your Children, in wayes, which tend to insnaring of them, as too many amongst Papists do their Children, in vowes of virginity

items.text: Do not require or encourage your children to take oppressing wages or prices or to follow proud, new-fangled fashions; instead train them in justice and modesty.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: put on your Children upon taking of oppressing wages & prices, upon new-fangled fashions

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. II. Of Honour in generall due to Parents.

items.text: Do not dishonor or reproach your parents in any way.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: A Son that any way dishonoureth, or reproacheth his Parents, shall be put under the rule of a servant

items.text: Receive your parents' instruction; do not refuse it.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: resuse instruction, especially of Parents

items.text: Do not curse your father or mother.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: forbidden Cursing of Father and Mother

items.text: Do not marry against your parents' minds; seek their consent in marriage.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: cross matching against their minds
items.conflict: Parents do not have absolute authority to choose spouses for adult children; Scripture requires mutual consent (1 Cor. 7:39).

items.text: Do not uncover your father's wife's nakedness or your mother's sister's nakedness; it dishonors your parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: The uncovering of a mans own Fathers wifes nakedness, or that of a mans own Mothers Sisters nakedness

items.text: Do not mock or expose your father's shame; cover his nakedness rather than make it a spectacle.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: derisive spectators and informers of old Noahs nakedness

items.text: Do not cast off your father's counsel, commands, rebukes, and watch; do not depart from his house like a vagrant.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: flung off his Fathers Counsels, commands, rebukes, and watch, and went from his Fathers house like a very vagrand

items.text: You who have children of your own still owe honor to your own father and mother; do not set before your children an example of dishonoring them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. II
items.quote: if Parents are vile towards their own naturall Fathers and Mothers, their Children commonly prove as bad

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.

items.text: Obey your parents' lawful commands even when tempted to disobey, overcoming the temptation as the Rechabites did.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: If when you are tempted to disobey your parents commands, yet you overcome the temptations, & obey your parents lawfull injunctions notwithstanding

items.text: Obey your parents' commands in matters unpleasant to the flesh, such as renouncing carnal delights, profits, or ease.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: obey your Parents command, in matters unpleasing to flesh and blood, and which cross you in matters of carnall delights, preferments, profits, or ease

items.text: Make filial obedience a lifelong habit, not just a single act, lasting all your days.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: habituated in a way of filial obedience to your Parents lawfull commands... but like that of obedient Rechabites lasting all your dayes

items.text: Propagate conscientious filial obedience to your own children when you become a parent.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: propagate conscientious filiall obedience to your posterity, when you are Parents

items.text: Obey your parents even if they are in a far meaner estate than yourself.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: filially obedient to parents lawfull injunctions, when your parents are in a far meaner estate, than you your selves are

items.text: Make your peace with God through faith and repentance, so that He may remove disobedience and irreverence from your household.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: Make your peace with God through faith in Jesus Christ... remove the iniquity of children also, as is disobedience and irreverence

items.text: As a parent, be exemplary in your own filial obedience and observance of your parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: Be you exemplary in wayes of filial obedience, and observance of your parents

items.text: Use your parental authority to command your children to obey God, curbing their disobedience.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. V. Of Honour of Obedience due to Parents.
items.quote: Inure your children to wayes of obedience unto the Lord, & be you frequently curbing their disobedience to Gods commands.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Use all your interests with God and men to seek their good, as they did for you.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. VI
items.quote: Let children, in way of recompence, improve their best interests either in God... for their good... or in men... to further... parentall good.

items.text: Supply their outward needs honorably, plentifully, readily, and freely, from your best, and sometimes before your own.
items.citation: Gouge, Honour due from Children to Parents, Chap. VI
items.quote: In supplying their outward wants: yet so as it be honourably, plentifully, readily, and freely, to their content, out of the very best, and in some cases before themselves.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. IV. Of Honour of Reverence due from children to Parents.

items.text: Give your parents the honor of reverence, both inward and outward.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Do you then strive, what in you lyeth, to give this Honour of Reverence, both outward and inward, which is due to your Parents.

items.text: Awe your parents, for they have parental power to bless or curse you.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: There is in your Parents some paternall power, if justly used, to bless and to curse you... and therefore the rather Awe your Parents.

items.text: Carry yourselves piously before your children, that they may reverence you.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Carry it very piously in your places, for that will gain awe in your inferiours, children or others.

items.text: Season your children early with principles of religion and their duty to God and parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Season your children betime with principles of religion, of their duty to God, to Parents, to others.

items.text: Bring your children often to the assemblies of God, where they may learn reverence to God and men.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Bring them oft to Gods aweful and awing Assemblies, where they will hear and learn Reverence to God or men.

items.text: Correct your children wisely and seasonably for irreverence to parents and other sins.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Correct them wisely and seasonably, as for other sins, so for those which savour of irreverence to Parents.

items.text: Acquaint your children often with God's dreadful judgments on children who did not reverence their parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Acquaint your Children ever and anon with Gods more awing and dreadfull providences, especially respecting Children, which gave not their Parents reverence.

items.text: Inure your children early to subjection and obedience to you as parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. IV
items.quote: Inure them to awfull subjection and obeysance to you as Parents, betimes.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Treat his good words as oracles of God: treasure them up, and in difficulty go first to him for counsel.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: be observing, minding, prising, and treasuring up such parents good speeches, as so many oracles of God

items.text: Make his parents’ breasts the first cabinet of every weighty secret; tell no one else before them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: to acquaint parents, in the first place, with all their Secrets, which are of weight

items.text: While under their tuition, ask their leave before taking any action, that their authority and wisdom be honored.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: To ask leave of their parents, at least whil'st Children are under their tuition, for what they do

items.text: When occasion offers, praise what is good in them; call them blessed as her children called the virtuous woman.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: Her Children rise up, and call her blessed

items.text: After they are gone, do all you can to keep their name from dishonor.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: maintain their names, even when they are dead, all they can

items.text: If any wrong or dishonor is done to them, take up their cause as far as your calling permits and set it right.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: vindicate any wrongs, injury, or dishonor done to parents, so far as it lyeth in the compass of Childrens calls

items.text: At their death give them all fitting honor: go up with them, bury them with solemn care, and let their funeral show your respect.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: Isaac and Ishmael, buried him in the Cave of Machpelah... Joseph went up to bury his Father

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Do not deride or wrong brothers or sisters whom your parents respect, for in so doing you trample your father's crown and glory.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: deride such of your godly Brethren, or Sisters, whom your Parents most respect... trample upon, and rend away their Fathers Crown, and Glory

items.text: Do not neglect the best time of your good under your parents' education, for that shames your parents and wastes the price in your hand.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: neglect the best time of your good, under the good education of your Parents... causeth shame, even to his very Parents

items.text: Do not join debauched companions or take up ruffianly customs, for that profanes your very good parents and shames your father's house.
items.citation: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, Chap. VII
items.quote: take to deboist company, and take up any Ruffianly customs or courses... profane your very good Parents

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Maintain a thankful remembrance of remarkable mercies extended to your parents, and cause posterity to keep it.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.7
items.quote: To maintain a thankfull remembrance of remarkable mercies extended to parents

items.text: Keep a thankful remembrance of remarkable mercies extended to your departed ancestors, and let posterity retain it.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.7
items.quote: remarkable mercies extended to parents, or Ancestors

items.text: Plead your parents' interest in the Lord and in His covenant in your prayers, by faith, thereby honoring them.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.8
items.quote: To improve godly persons interest in the Lord, and in his Covenant, by faith, and to plead them in their prayers

items.text: Imitate all the grace and virtues you saw in your parents: faith, love, holiness, patience, and the like.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.9
items.quote: To imitate all that good of grace, as of faith, love, and holiness, righteousness, patience

items.text: Do not apostatize or degenerate from the faith, truth, worship, and ways your parents held forth to you.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.10
items.quote: Not to suffer themselves to be drawn aside, or to Apostatise, or degenerate from that of God and Christ, and his grace, truth, worship and wayes, which their Parents have

items.text: Honor all that is honourable in your mother-in-law, as Ruth honored Naomi: her God, her faith, her people.
items.citation: Honour due from Children 7.9
items.quote: Thy God shall be my God, and thy people my people

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VI. Of Honour of Recompence or thankefulness due to Parents.

items.text: Communicate to your parents of the blessings of this life which God gives you, according as they have need.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: communicate to their parents, of the blessings of this life... according as their parents at any time may need

items.text: Relieve a widowed mother abundantly, honourably, and sufficiently, as part of honouring father and mother.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: let him abundantly supply their wants, or let him minister enough to them

items.text: Do not be a grief to your parents by lewd courses; be their joy and gladness.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.

items.text: Do not rob your father or mother, nor waste their estate by secret excess, gaming, or company-keeping.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother... is the companion of a destroyer.

items.text: Do not be hard-hearted or cruel to your brothers and sisters, for such unkindness is reckoned as unkindness to your parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Unkindness to Children being ever reckoned, as unkindnesse offered to Fathers.

items.text: Do not betray your parents to persecutors or strike them; such inhumanity is punishable by death.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: He that striketh Father or Mother shall die.

items.text: Take special care to leave your children the good blessings of God for their souls' welfare, that they may be engaged to requite you.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Take speciall care to leave your children the good blessings of God, respecting their souls welfare.

items.text: Use lawful industry and providence to establish your children in callings and with portions so they can support you.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Use all lawfull meanes, industry, and providence to leave your Children in such places, and in such callings... that they may be inabled to discharge such a duty.

items.text: Teach your children principles of gratitude to others, especially to their progenitors, and curb ingratitude in them.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Distil into your children principles of gratitude to others, especially unto progenitors.

items.text: Be an example to your children by honouring and recompensing your own parents.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Be you exemplary to your Children, in this gratefull recompence of your Parents.

items.text: Protect your godly children from harm; do not shield off blows from them, nor betray them or undermine their safety.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: Be it far from you to be so ungracious towards your godly children, as not to shield off blowes from them... much less... to undermine their childrens safety or liberty.

items.text: Do not waste your own estate through dissolute living, lest you be disabled from helping your parents in their need.
items.citation: Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse, CHAP. VI
items.quote: deboist youngsters, who by their dissolute courses wast their estates, whereby they might have ministred to Parents wants afterwards.

work: A Fruitfull and Usefull Discourse touching the Honour due from Children to Paren
heading: CHAP. VII. Of Honour in a Reflect way due from Children unto Parents.

items.text: Follow your parents' godly precepts and examples; do not turn aside from the ways they taught you.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: walk not after the precepts, which they often gave you, nor in the blessed paths wherein they exemplary led you

items.text: Honor your godly ancestors by continuing in the faith they held and walking in the paths they trod, not forsaking the Lord God of your fathers.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: they forsook the Lord God of their Fathers—they turned quickly out of the way, which their Fathers walked in

items.text: Bring up your children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, training them in the way they should go.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord

items.text: Train your children in the holy Scriptures from childhood, so that they may be wise for salvation.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: Train up a Child in the way that he should go

items.text: Correct your children and do not withhold the rod, for folly is bound up in a child's heart and correction will drive it far from him.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him

items.text: Teach your children diligently the words of God, and put them early upon the practice of prayer, Bible reading, and Sabbath-keeping.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: thou shalt teach these words diligently to thy Children, when thou sittest in thine house

items.text: If your children have aptitude for learning, set them apart for education, especially for the ministry of the church.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: such of your Children as may be men capable of learning, let parents set them apart for learning

items.text: Take special care in arranging the marriages of your sons and daughters.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: take speciall care of the well disposing of their Sons and Daughters, in Matiage

items.text: Give your children their portions and settle them so as to maintain peace among them and prevent future strife.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: maintain peace among their Children, and to take away all occasion of breaches among them

items.text: Leave your children under the pure ordinances of God and good civil government.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: leave your Children under Gods ordinances purely & powerfully dispensed

items.text: Pray for your children and exercise faith in God's promises for their spiritual good.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: lay up many prayers for them, for that end, and accordingly exercise faith also in Gods promises

items.text: Hearken to the admonitions and entreaties of your parents; do not despise their tears and prayers for your salvation.
items.citation: Fruitfull Discourse, CHAP. VII
items.quote: Ah dear Son, dear Daughter, that you would once at length look out seriously, after the salvation of your souls
